items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Count thought that maybe they should get someone else to help do some of that. That’s when he asked me to join the band, in 1954.

ctx.x: How did you join Count Basie’s band?

I was playing – what was I . . . ? I was doing a show. What show was I doing? I remember I left the theater. I’m not sure whether I was doing – 1954. Was I doing The Most Happy Fella? Oh, oh no no. I think – I’m trying to remember now how I got there. Oh, I know. I got a call from Count Basie, because they wanted – Joe Newman was in the band, and he was playing most of the trumpet solos, all the improvising, and it was getting to be a little too much for him alone. items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: And Basie was looking for someone and that’s how I came to join the band.

ctx.x: How did the gig with Basie come about? It’s usually word of mouth, isn’t it, that leads somewhere?

Well I knew Basie and I knew a lot of people in the band. But Joe Newman was the featured trumpet soloist basically. He played most of the trumpet solos, not all of them, but he was working so much and he said that they needed to get someone else to take some of the load off of him. And Basie was looking for someone and that’s how I came to join the band. And it was actually, to take a little of the pressure off Joe.
Did you get a lot of his solos?

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: The Count was so relaxed and so nice, he was a nice man, and the band was such a swinging band. I didn’t stay with them long, I wasn’t with them very long, but I enjoyed all the time that I was with them.

ctx.x: Is there one band or orchestra or circumstance that you missed that you could go back to if you could turn back the clock?

I guess, well you know I loved Basie’s band. The Count was so relaxed and so nice, he was a nice man, and the band was such a swinging band. I didn’t stay with them long, I wasn’t with them very long, but I enjoyed all the time that I was with them. And Jimmy Lunceford’s band, I was so sorry that he passed away because the band was coming back and the guys he had in the band were good players and it was reaching a point where the band was really beginning to develop on the same level as the original band, which…
